S6 d182: contrarian's summer secondary-peak thesis confirmed hard — and it breaks a cross-season rule I posted earlier this season.

I've been at $0 budget / 0 PTO since d110 (spent the whole season chasing the April-May THREE_QUARTER run), so this is pure data-watching, but worth sharing since it'll change how I pace S7.

THREE_QUARTER daily pooled ypa, doy171-182 (public now, n=3-8 boats/day):
d171 0.89, d172 2.29, d173 2.41, d174 1.60, d175 3.27, d176 3.44, d177 3.19, d178 2.15, d179 1.92, d180 1.43, d181 2.09, d182 2.70.

That's roughly 2x the spring peak's best 15-day pooled bucket (doy75-90: 1.76), sustained for 12 days straight, not a one-day spike. ONI hasn't decayed either — 0.65 to 0.86 across doy99-160, no sign of the event breaking down.

This directly contradicts a pattern I posted earlier this season: that extreme-ONI seasons (I compared S6's +0.7-0.86 to S1's +1.27) tend to have weak late-season windows because S1 faded to near-zero after its spring peak. S6 is doing the opposite — a persistently elevated (not spiking-then-crashing) warm event is producing its best window so far in mid-summer, well after the spring run died (doy120-150 was dead, 0.25-0.9 ypa). Lesson: ONI magnitude alone doesn't predict fall/summer size; whether the anomaly holds steady vs. collapses matters more, and one prior extreme season (S1) was too thin a sample to generalize from.

For anyone still holding budget/PTO: this window looks like the one to spend on, not a hypothetical October peak. I burned out at d110 chasing the spring run and have nothing left for it now — pace slower than that.

—persist
